questions.stem: A grain silo is shaped like a right circular cylinder with a hemisphere on top. The cylinder and the hemisphere each have a radius of 5 meters, and the cylinder is 12 meters tall. What is the total volume of the silo, in cubic meters? (The volume of a sphere of radius r is (4/3)πr³.)
questions.explanation: Cylinder: πr²h = π(25)(12) = 300π. Hemisphere: half of (4/3)π(125) = (2/3)(125)π = 250π/3. Total: 300π + 250π/3 = 900π/3 + 250π/3 = 1150π/3 (about 1,204 cubic meters).

distractor_explanations.A: 300π is the cylinder alone; the hemisphere was left out.
distractor_explanations.C: This uses πr³ = 125π for the hemisphere instead of (2/3)πr³.
distractor_explanations.D: This adds a whole sphere, 500π/3, instead of half a sphere.

hints: Find the two volumes separately, then add.
A hemisphere is half of a sphere.
questions.remember: Composite solids: add the volumes of the parts.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, point D lies on side AB and point E lies on side AC so that segment DE is parallel to side BC. AD = 6 and DB = 4. The area of triangle ADE is 54 square units. What is the area, in square units, of quadrilateral DBCE?
questions.explanation: Because DE ∥ BC, triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC with scale factor AD/AB = 6/10 = 3/5. Areas scale by (3/5)² = 9/25, so the area of ABC is 54 × 25/9 = 150. The quadrilateral DBCE is ABC minus ADE: 150 − 54 = 96.

distractor_explanations.A: This uses the ratio DB/AD = 4/6 and squares it: 54 × (4/6)² = 24. DB is not a side of either similar triangle.
distractor_explanations.B: This scales area by the linear ratio 10/6 (area of ABC = 90) and subtracts 54.
distractor_explanations.D: 150 is the area of the whole triangle ABC; the area of ADE still has to be subtracted.

hints: Which two triangles are similar, and what is the ratio of their corresponding sides?
Areas of similar figures scale by the square of the side ratio.

strategy.explanation: Sketch the triangle with DE across it; AB = 10, so ratio 3/5, area ratio 9/25; find ABC, then subtract ADE.

questions.remember: Similar figures: area ratio is the side ratio squared.

questions.stem: A carnival game costs $2 to play. On each play, a player wins a $10 prize with probability 0.1, wins a $4 prize with probability 0.2, and wins nothing otherwise. What is the expected net gain for a player per play, taking the cost to play into account?
questions.explanation: Expected prize = 10(0.1) + 4(0.2) + 0(0.7) = 1.00 + 0.80 = $1.80. Subtract the $2 cost: 1.80 − 2.00 = −$0.20 per play, an expected loss of 20 cents.

distractor_explanations.B: $1.80 is the expected prize; the $2 cost has not been subtracted.
distractor_explanations.C: This averages the three outcomes $10, $4 and $0 equally and subtracts $2, ignoring the probabilities.
distractor_explanations.D: This adds the $2 cost to the expected prize instead of subtracting it.

hints: Multiply each prize by its probability and add.
Net gain means prizes minus what the player pays.

strategy.explanation: E = Σ(value × probability) − cost = 1.80 − 2.00.

questions.remember: Expected value weights each outcome by its probability.

questions.stem: Each of the following data sets has a mean of 5. Which data set has the greatest standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation measures how far the values typically are from the mean. All four sets have mean 5. In set C, two values are 4 units from the mean; in the other sets the values are at most 2 units away. Set C is the most spread out.

distractor_explanations.A: Every value equals the mean, so the standard deviation is 0, the least possible.
distractor_explanations.B: The values are at most 1 unit from the mean, so this set has little spread.
distractor_explanations.D: The values are at most 2 units from the mean, less spread than set C.

hints: Standard deviation measures spread around the mean.
Which set has values farthest from 5?

strategy.explanation: No calculation needed: compare how far each set's values are from 5.

questions.remember: More spread from the mean means a larger standard deviation.

questions.stem: On a 420-mile trip, Lena drove 300 miles on highways and the remaining miles in cities. Her car averaged 30 miles per gallon on highways and 20 miles per gallon in cities. Gasoline cost $3.60 per gallon. What was the total cost of the gasoline used on the trip?
questions.explanation: Highway: 300 ÷ 30 = 10 gallons. City: 120 ÷ 20 = 6 gallons. Total: 16 gallons × $3.60 = $57.60.

distractor_explanations.A: This uses the highway rate for the whole trip: 420 ÷ 30 = 14 gallons, costing $50.40.
distractor_explanations.C: This averages the two mileage rates (25 miles per gallon): 420 ÷ 25 = 16.8 gallons, costing $60.48. The rates apply to different distances.
distractor_explanations.D: This uses the city rate for the whole trip: 420 ÷ 20 = 21 gallons, costing $75.60.

hints: Find the gallons used on each part of the trip separately.
How many miles were driven in cities?

strategy.explanation: Gallons = 300/30 + 120/20 = 16; multiply by $3.60.

questions.remember: Different rates for different parts: compute each part separately.
